blindSummary: This state/province combines mob 'community justice' with active secular policing. In April 2018, two men were stripped naked, beaten and paraded through the streets of a town by a crowd accusing them of gay sex. In February 2025, the state/province police command announced it had 'foiled a same-sex party' at a hotel in a district of the state capital, arresting multiple gay and lesbian suspects, and explicitly named the 14-year penalty under the anti-same-sex statute. The pattern across years and modality (mob then state) supports a regional finding rather than isolated stories: the 2025 operation is direct state enforcement naming the criminal law, while the 2018 parade is community violence met without accountability.
blindSourceSummaries: An LGBTQ+ news outlet's report (26 April 2018): two men in this state/province were stripped naked, beaten and paraded through the streets of a town with palm leaves tied round them after being accused of gay sex, by a crowd that filmed and shouted at them; a third man escaped, and a follow-up inquiry reported the two were taken by police. The outlet situates the attack in a rising pattern of mob justice enabled by the 2014 anti-gay law.

A national news outlet's report (19 February 2025): the state/province police command announced it had stormed a 'same-sex party' at a hotel in a district of the state capital on 15 February 2025 after a hotel tip-off, arresting eight suspects (four women, four men) and charging them under the anti-gay law the command cited as carrying a 14-year term; the command's briefing expressly framed enforcement against 'gay, lesbian, bisexual and/or transgender act', with fleeers still being sought.
